_comment: 1987 Chevrolet Camaro IROC-Z coupe, 5.7 L L98 TPI V8 (R&T test car: 220 bhp), 700R4 four-speed automatic, 3.27 Borg-Warner axle with cone limited slip, P245/50VR16 Goodyear Eagle VR50, four-wheel discs, no ABS. Model: Sketchfab '1985 Chevrolet Camaro IROC-Z' by Tony (tonyferello), CC BY 4.0.
name: Camaro IROC-Z 5.7

card.handling: Road & Track (Oct 1986): 0.85 g on a 150 ft skidpad, 63.3 mph slalom; stiffly sprung, more stable under braking than the Mustang GT; less precise on centre.

sources.calibration: Road & Track, October 1986, Mustang GT vs Camaro IROC-Z (1987 models), thirdgen.org reprint: 0-60 6.8 s, 1/4 mile 15.3 s at 90.5 mph, 60-0 159 ft, 80-0 261 ft, 0.85 g on a 75 ft radius skidpad, 63.3 mph slalom, 149 mph. 70-0 208 ft derived from the two stops.
sources.engine: R&T test car: 220 bhp at 4200 rpm, 320 lb-ft at 3200 rpm (production 1987 rating 225 hp at 4400, 330 lb-ft; secondary). Curve shape, idle and fuel cut are estimates. Firing order 1-8-4-3-6-5-7-2.
sources.gearing: 700R4 3.06/1.63/1.00/0.70, converter 1.8:1, 3.27 axle (R&T); reverse 2.29 (secondary). R&T's 33.1 mph/1000 rpm in 4th matches the tyre size.
sources.chassis: 3,490 lb curb, 58/42, 101.0 in wheelbase, 60.7/60.6 in track, 192.0 x 72.8 x 50.3 in (R&T).
sources.aero: Cd 0.34 x 21 ft2 (forum, secondary); CdA 0.66 m2 is consistent with 149 mph on 220 bhp.
sources.estimates: CG height, inertia, wheel rates (1.45/1.55 Hz), dampers, brake torques and proportioning, LSD bias, engine friction and pumping, alignment, turning circle, launch and shift points.

calibration_open: Skidpad target is from a 150 ft diameter pad, not 300 ft. 70-0 is derived. The engine curve shape is an estimate between two published points. Spring and bar data not found. 0-60: the bench floors the throttle from rest, and 434 N m through the 1.8:1 converter and 3.06 first spins the 245/50R16 rears (slip over 1 to 33 mph), so the bench reads about 8.6 s; Road & Track's 6.8 s was a driver feeding the throttle in. The IROC-Z had no traction control, so the car keeps none; a player who eases on gets the real launch.
